parsed.attack: Every piece of evidence here is a person reporting guilt - 'forget a person exists for months and then dislike themselves for it' - and guilt is the most abundant and least convertible feeling in consumer software. The product's output is a number the user already possesses: nobody fails to call their mother because they were unsure it had been 34 days, they fail because calling is effortful and the feeling is avoidant, and a lock-screen counter raises the cost of avoidance without lowering the cost of calling. The category has already been answered empirically and repeatedly - the keep-in-touch app that closed in April 2026, the contacts apps acqui-hired and switched off, and Google's own Assistant Snapshot, which had the best data, the best models and default placement on every Android phone and was shut down because nobody engaged with the proactive card.
parsed.strongest_defence: Prior products failed by being databases with upkeep, birthdays and streak pressure; this one has no list to maintain, three people maximum, and stays silent on any day contact already happened, so the only thing a user ever sees is one actionable button at the single moment they are off work and free.
parsed.verdict_reason: The evidence is self-reported guilt about a fact the user already knows, and every product that tried to convert this exact feeling into a subscription has died, including one with default placement on every Android phone.
